comparisonScope: Exactly matched physical inputs, schedules, precision and resource limits; only subdivisions differ.
Exact rational differences/sums of stored binary64 values with 120-digit square roots for displayed norms.
Fixed 2 ms endpoints support cross-pair comparisons. Additional 1/0.5/0.25 ms common endpoints can expose missed peaks; no interpolation or alignment.
Native velocities and secants over the specified common window remain distinct.
Apparent order is an observed successive-discrepancy ratio, not an error guarantee or garment/material validation.
findings: All physical inputs, force criteria, precision, runtime and resource limits match. Only subdivisions differ; all four runs complete with zero rejected attempts.
Fixed 2 ms maximum position discrepancies are 3.84669, 7.19700 and 5.24359 micrometres for successive adjacent pairs; all occur at 64 ms. The sequence is not monotone.

On the same fixed 2 ms endpoints, native-velocity discrepancy grows from 1.27284 to 2.32116 to 3.81542 mm/s. Common 2 ms displacement secants improve from 1.06975 to 0.583850 to 0.293874 mm/s; averaging does not establish native-velocity convergence.
The finest common 1 ms grid exposes a 5.35569 micrometre early 64/128 position discrepancy at 1 ms, missed by the former 2 ms grid. The earlier tail-dominance claim applies only to that sampled grid.
With finest common windows of 1/0.5/0.25 ms, peak secant differences are 5.85388/6.07906/6.71567 mm/s. These use different observables and cannot define a cross-pair convergence rate.
Final maximum speeds rise from 0.999600 through 1.300440 and 1.674184 to 1.880015 mm/s. Every saved state moves. No physical settling or material damping is established.

Recorded contact entry occurs at 1/1.5/1.75/1.75 ms and exit at 35/34.5/34.25/34.375 ms. These are endpoint observations, not exact event times. Native speed peaks and velocity differences remain sensitive near engagement.
Net discrete parameter work is positive but nonmonotone across grids: approximately 11.4383/11.1439/11.2180/11.4476 nJ. Response/work error bounds are not temporal trajectory-error bounds.
